items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: Willie and Lewis Dover, had a band. And I heard of it, and they had heard of me. So we got together.

ctx.x: So you were nine when they gave you the coronet.

Oh, that was music. And he was very good, that Professor Young. He taught basic music. And I was eager to learn, and he said I was a good pupil. And I learned how to play coronet from him. Well, I went very religiously and regularly to the rehearsals, and I learned to play. And I used to practice at home. They let me play until they got tired and told me to stop that noise, and I had to stop.

Well, that was downtown. We slowly moved uptown. This is Manhattten, and I became acquainted with some older fellows, and a boys band was two young fellows. Willie and Lewis Dover, had a band. And I heard of it, and they had heard of me. So we got together. It was a nice little band, young fellows, very young. And we rehearsed together very religiously and all that kind of - we got work.
